tool.name: OpenSwathWorkflow
tool.command:
@QUOTE_FOO@ @EXT_FOO@ #import re
## Preprocessing mkdir in && cp '$in' 'in/${gxy_input_basename($in.element_identifier, $in.ext)}' && mkdir tr && cp '$tr' 'tr/${gxy_input_basename($tr.element_identifier, $tr.ext)}' && #if $swath_windows_file: mkdir swath_windows_file && cp '$swath_windows_file' 'swath_windows_file/${gxy_input_basename($swath_windows_file.element_identifier, $swath_windows_file.ext)}' && #end if #if "out_features_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_features && #end if #if "out_chrom_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_chrom && #end if #if "out_mobilogram_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_mobilogram && #end if #if "out_qc_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_qc && #end if #if "irt_mzml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir Debugging_irt_mzml && #end if #if "irt_trafo_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir Debugging_irt_trafo && #end if #if $Calibration.rt_norm: mkdir Calibration.rt_norm && cp '$Calibration.rt_norm' 'Calibration.rt_norm/${gxy_input_basename($Calibration.rt_norm.element_identifier, $Calibration.rt_norm.ext)}' && #end if
## Main program call
set -o pipefail && @EXECUTABLE@ -write_ctd ./ && python3 '$__tool_directory__/fill_ctd.py' '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$args_json' '$hardcoded_json' && @EXECUTABLE@ -ini @EXECUTABLE@.ctd -in 'in/${gxy_input_basename($in.element_identifier, $in.ext)}' -tr 'tr/${gxy_input_basename($tr.element_identifier, $tr.ext)}' #if $swath_windows_file: -swath_windows_file 'swath_windows_file/${gxy_input_basename($swath_windows_file.element_identifier, $swath_windows_file.ext)}' #end if #if "out_features_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_features 'out_features/output.${out_features_type}' #end if #if "out_chrom_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_chrom 'out_chrom/output.${adv_opts.out_chrom_type}' #end if #if "out_mobilogram_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_mobilogram 'out_mobilogram/output.${gxy2omsext("binary")}' #end if #if "out_qc_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_qc 'out_qc/output.${gxy2omsext("json")}' #end if #if "irt_mzml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -Debugging:irt_mzml 'Debugging_irt_mzml/output.${gxy2omsext("mzml")}' #end if #if "irt_trafo_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -Debugging:irt_trafo 'Debugging_irt_trafo/output.${gxy2omsext("trafoxml")}' #end if #if $Calibration.rt_norm: -Calibration:rt_norm 'Calibration.rt_norm/${gxy_input_basename($Calibration.rt_norm.element_identifier, $Calibration.rt_norm.ext)}' #end if #if len(str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',')) == 0 | tee '$stdout' #end if
## Postprocessing #if "out_features_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out_features/output.${out_features_type}' '$out_features' #end if #if "out_chrom_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out_chrom/output.${adv_opts.out_chrom_type}' '$out_chrom' #end if #if "out_mobilogram_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out_mobilogram/output.${gxy2omsext("binary")}' '$out_mobilogram' #end if #if "out_qc_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out_qc/output.${gxy2omsext("json")}' '$out_qc' #end if #if "irt_mzml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'Debugging_irt_mzml/output.${gxy2omsext("mzml")}' '$Debugging_irt_mzml' #end if #if "irt_trafo_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'Debugging_irt_trafo/output.${gxy2omsext("trafoxml")}' '$Debugging_irt_trafo' #end if #if "ctd_out_FLAG" in $OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS && mv '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$ctd_out' #end if

section.name: Calibration
section.title: Parameters for calibrant iRT peptides for RT normalization and mass / ion mobility correction, including configurable estimated RT-window floor/ceiling clamps

param.name: tr_irt_priority_sampling
param.label: Optional custom transition file (TSV format only) containing additional priority peptides for iRT sampling
param.help: These peptides will be prioritized alongside the built-in irtkit and cirtkit peptides when `auto_irt` is enabled. Useful for including project-specific or custom iRT peptides

param.name: rt_norm
param.label: RT normalization file (how to map the RTs of this run to the ones stored in the library)
param.help: If set, tr_irt may be omitted select trafoxml,traml data sets(s)

param.name: enabled
param.label: Whether to sample iRTs on‐the‐fly (true) from the input targeted transition file (instead of passing specific iRT files)
param.help: This may be useful if standard iRTs (Biognosys iRT kit) were not spiked-in. If set to false, and no additional iRT files are provided, and no transformation is provided, then no calibration is performed

param.name: irt_bins
param.label: Number of RT bins for linear iRT sampling

param.name: irt_peptides_per_bin
param.label: Peptides sampled per bin for linear iRT

param.name: irt_seed
param.label: RNG seed for reproducible sampling (0 = non-deterministic)

param.name: irt_bins_nonlinear
param.label: Number of RT bins for nonlinear iRT sampling

param.name: irt_peptides_per_bin_nonlinear
param.label: Peptides sampled per bin for nonlinear iRT (0 = skip nonlinear)

param.name: linear_top_fraction
param.label: Top fraction of intense peptides to sample for linear iRT

param.name: nonlinear_top_fraction
param.label: Top fraction of intense peptides to sample for nonlinear iRT

param.name: irt_nonlinear_rt_extraction_window
param.label: Only extract RT around this value for non linear iRT calibration (set to -1 to use whole range)

param.name: enabled
param.label: Enable raw-data evidence prefiltering for sampled iRT peptides

param.name: evidence_sources
param.label: Evidence source for iRT prefiltering: use MS2 fragments only (more stringent than hybrid)

param.name: ms1_top_peaks_per_spectrum
param.label: Number of most intense MS1 peaks to keep per spectrum before precursor m/z matching

param.name: ms2_top_peaks_per_spectrum
param.label: Number of most intense MS2 peaks to keep per spectrum before fragment m/z matching

param.name: ms2_top_transitions_per_precursor
param.label: Number of highest library-intensity fragment transitions to index per precursor for MS2 evidence

param.name: ms2_min_fragment_hits
param.label: Minimum fragment hits for iRT prefiltering (higher threshold ensures robust iRT peptides)

param.name: min_supported_precursors
param.label: Minimum number of supported precursors required when the prefilter is enabled

param.name: enabled
param.label: Run PeakPickerHiRes on spectra before top-N matching
param.help: This is intended for profile data and is disabled by default

param.name: use_gauss
param.label: Use Gaussian smoothing before PeakPickerHiRes
param.help: If false, use Savitzky-Golay smoothing

param.name: signal_to_noise
param.label: Minimal signal-to-noise ratio for a peak to be picked (0.0 disables SNT estimation!)

param.name: spacing_difference_gap
param.label: The extension of a peak is stopped if the spacing between two subsequent data points exceeds 'spacing_difference_gap * min_spacing'
param.help: 'min_spacing' is the smaller of the two spacings from the peak apex to its two neighboring points. '0' to disable the constraint. Not applicable to chromatograms

param.name: spacing_difference
param.label: Maximum allowed difference between points during peak extension, in multiples of the minimal difference between the peak apex and its two neighboring points
param.help: If this difference is exceeded a missing point is assumed (see parameter 'missing'). A higher value implies a less stringent peak definition, since individual signals within the peak are allowed to be further apart. '0' to disable the constraint. Not applicable to chromatograms

param.name: missing
param.label: Maximum number of missing points allowed when extending a peak to the left or to the right
param.help: A missing data point occurs if the spacing between two subsequent data points exceeds 'spacing_difference * min_spacing'. 'min_spacing' is the smaller of the two spacings from the peak apex to its two neighboring points. Not applicable to chromatograms

param.name: ms_levels
param.label: List of MS levels for which the peak picking is applied
param.help: If empty, auto mode is enabled, all peaks which aren't picked yet will get picked. Other scans are copied to the output without changes (space separated list, in order to allow for spaces in list items surround them by single quotes)

expand.name: ms_levels

validator.message: a space separated list of integer values in the range 1: is required

expand.validator: len(value.split(' ')) == len([_ for _ in value.split(' ') if 1 <= int(_)])

param.name: report_FWHM
param.label: Add metadata for FWHM (as floatDataArray named 'FWHM' or 'FWHM_ppm', depending on param 'report_FWHM_unit') for each picked peak

param.name: report_FWHM_unit
param.label: Unit of FWHM
param.help: Either absolute in the unit of input, e.g. 'm/z' for spectra, or relative as ppm (only sensible for spectra, not chromatograms)

param.name: allow_missing_flank
param.label: Allow peaks without flanking data points on both sides
param.help: This is useful for TimsTOF data where profile peaks may be missing the leading or trailing edge

param.name: max_intensity
param.label: maximal intensity considered for histogram construction
param.help: By default, it will be calculated automatically (see auto_mode). Only provide this parameter if you know what you are doing (and change 'auto_mode' to '-1')! All intensities EQUAL/ABOVE 'max_intensity' will be added to the LAST histogram bin. If you choose 'max_intensity' too small, the noise estimate might be too small as well. If chosen too big, the bins become quite large (which you could counter by increasing 'bin_count', which increases runtime). In general, the Median-S/N estimator is more robust to a manual max_intensity than the MeanIterative-S/N

param.name: auto_max_stdev_factor
param.label: parameter for 'max_intensity' estimation (if 'auto_mode' == 0): mean + 'auto_max_stdev_factor' * stdev

param.name: auto_max_percentile
param.label: parameter for 'max_intensity' estimation (if 'auto_mode' == 1): auto_max_percentile th percentile

param.name: auto_mode
param.label: method to use to determine maximal intensity: -1 --> use 'max_intensity'; 0 --> 'auto_max_stdev_factor' method (default); 1 --> 'auto_max_percentile' method

param.name: win_len
param.label: window length in Thomson

param.name: bin_count
param.label: number of bins for intensity values

param.name: min_required_elements
param.label: minimum number of elements required in a window (otherwise it is considered sparse)

param.name: noise_for_empty_window
param.label: noise value used for sparse windows

param.name: write_log_messages
param.label: Write out log messages in case of sparse windows or median in rightmost histogram bin

param.name: linear_irt_file
param.label: Path(s) to linear iRT transition file(s) (TraML, TSV, or PQP)
param.help: Accepts a string of a single file path or multiple file paths (space-separated, 'run1_irt.pqp run2_irt.pqp ... runN_irt.pqp') for run-specific mapping (positional: nth entry -> nth run)

param.name: nonlinear_irt_file
param.label: Path(s) to nonlinear iRT transition file(s) (TraML, TSV, or PQP)
param.help: Accepts a string of a single file path or multiple file paths (space-separated, 'run1_irt.pqp run2_irt.pqp ... runN_irt.pqp') for run-specific mapping (positional: nth entry -> nth run). Entries may be empty to indicate no nonlinear iRT for that run

param.name: outlier_detection
param.label: Which outlier detection method to use for linear calibration (valid: 'iter_residual', 'iter_jackknife', 'ransac', 'none')
param.help: Iterative methods remove one outlier at a time. Jackknife approach optimizes for maximum r-squared improvement while 'iter_residual' removes the datapoint with the largest residual error (removal by residual is computationally cheaper, use this with lots of peptides)

param.name: outlier_detection
param.label: Which outlier detection method to use for nonlinear calibration (valid: 'iter_residual', 'iter_jackknife', 'ransac', 'none')
param.help: Iterative methods remove one outlier at a time. Jackknife approach optimizes for maximum r-squared improvement while 'iter_residual' removes the datapoint with the largest residual error (removal by residual is computationally cheaper, use this with lots of peptides)

param.name: estimate_rt
param.label: Estimate RT extraction windows from calibration

param.name: estimate_mz
param.label: Estimate m/z extraction windows from calibration

param.name: estimate_im
param.label: Estimate ion mobility extraction windows from calibration

param.name: rt_percentile
param.label: Percentile for RT window estimation (25.0-99.9)

param.name: rt_estimation_padding_factor
param.label: A padding factor to multiply the estimated RT window by
param.help: For example, a factor of 1.3 will add a 30% padding to the estimated RT window, so if the estimated RT window is 144, then 43 will be added for a total estimated RT window of 187 seconds. A factor of 1.0 will not add any padding to the estimated window

param.name: min_rt_window
param.label: Minimum RT extraction window in seconds to apply after RT-window estimation
param.help: Set to 0 to disable the floor and use the raw estimated RT window

param.name: max_rt_window
param.label: Maximum RT extraction window in seconds to apply after RT-window estimation
param.help: Set to 0 to disable the ceiling and use the raw estimated RT window

param.name: min_rsq
param.label: Minimum R-squared required for RT peptides regression

param.name: min_coverage
param.label: Minimum relative amount of RT peptides to keep

section.name: RTNormalization
section.title: Parameters for the RTNormalization for iRT peptides
section.help: This specifies how the RT alignment is performed and how outlier detection is applied. Outlier detection can be done iteratively (by default) which removes one outlier per iteration or using the RANSAC algorithm

param.name: alignmentMethod
param.label: How to perform the alignment to the normalized RT space using anchor points
param.help: 'linear': perform linear regression (for few anchor points). 'interpolated': Interpolate between anchor points (for few, noise-free anchor points). 'lowess' Use local regression (for many, noisy anchor points). 'b_spline' use b splines for smoothing

param.name: useIterativeChauvenet
param.label: Whether to use Chauvenet's criterion when using iterative methods
param.help: This should be used if the algorithm removes too many datapoints but it may lead to true outliers being retained

param.name: RANSACMaxIterations
param.label: Maximum iterations for the RANSAC outlier detection algorithm

param.name: RANSACMaxPercentRTThreshold
param.label: Maximum threshold in RT dimension for the RANSAC outlier detection algorithm (in percent of the total gradient)
param.help: Default is set to 3% which is around +/- 4 minutes on a 120 gradient

param.name: RANSACSamplingSize
param.label: Sampling size of data points per iteration for the RANSAC outlier detection algorithm

param.name: estimateBestPeptides
param.label: Whether the algorithms should try to choose the best peptides based on their peak shape for normalization
param.help: Use this option you do not expect all your peptides to be detected in a sample and too many 'bad' peptides enter the outlier removal step (e.g. due to them being endogenous peptides or using a less curated list of peptides)

param.name: InitialQualityCutoff
param.label: The initial overall quality cutoff for a peak to be scored (range ca

param.name: OverallQualityCutoff
param.label: The overall quality cutoff for a peak to go into the retention time estimation (range ca

param.name: NrRTBins
param.label: Number of RT bins to use to compute coverage
param.help: This option should be used to ensure that there is a complete coverage of the RT space (this should detect cases where only a part of the RT gradient is actually covered by normalization peptides)

param.name: MinPeptidesPerBin
param.label: Minimal number of peptides that are required for a bin to counted as 'covered'

param.name: MinBinsFilled
param.label: Minimal number of bins required to be covered

param.name: auto_span

param.label: Whether to write out all points of all features into the featureXML

param.name: spectrum_addition_method
param.label: For spectrum addition, either use simple concatenation or use peak resampling

param.name: spectrum_merge_method_type
param.label: For spectrum addition, either use a fixed number of spectra or dynamically select the number of spectra to add around the peak apex based on the merge_spectra_by_peak_width_fraction

param.name: add_up_spectra
param.label: Add up spectra on the left and right around the retention time peak apex

param.name: spacing_for_spectra_resampling
param.label: If spectra are to be added, use this spacing to add them up

param.name: merge_spectra_by_peak_width_fraction
param.label: If spectra are to be added based on the peak width of peak, construct number of spectra to be added based on N percent of number of points of peak width

param.name: uis_threshold_sn
param.label: S/N threshold to consider identification transition (set to -1 to consider all)

param.name: uis_threshold_peak_area
param.label: Peak area threshold to consider identification transition (set to -1 to consider all)

param.name: scoring_model
param.label: Scoring model to use

param.name: im_extra_drift
param.label: Extra drift time to extract for IM scoring (as a fraction
param.help: e.g. 0.25 means 25% extra on each side)

param.name: strict
param.label: Whether to error (true) or skip (false) if a transition in a transition group does not have a corresponding chromatogram

param.name: use_ms1_ion_mobility
param.label: Performs ion mobility extraction in MS1
param.help: Set to false if MS1 spectra do not contain ion mobility

param.name: apply_im_peak_picking
param.label: Perform peak picking on the extracted ion mobilograms
param.help: This is useful for reducing intefering signals from co-eluting analytes in the ion mobility dimension. The peak picking will take the highest peak and discard the remaining peaks for ion mobility scoring.

param.name: enzyme
param.label: Enzyme used for counting missed cleavages in peptide sequences

param.name: mz_extraction_window
param.label: m/z extraction window (full width) to be used for matching/extraction
param.help: If -1, defaults in workflow will be used

param.name: mz_extraction_window_unit
param.label: Unit for mz_extraction_window: 'Th' or 'ppm'

param.name: mz_extraction_window_ms1
param.label: m/z extraction window for MS1 (full width)
param.help: If -1, defaults in workflow will be used

param.name: mz_extraction_window_ms1_unit
param.label: Unit for mz_extraction_window_ms1: 'Th' or 'ppm'

param.name: irt_mz_extraction_window
param.label: m/z extraction window (full width) to be used specifically for iRT matching/extraction
param.help: If -1, defaults in workflow will be used

param.name: irt_mz_extraction_window_unit
param.label: Unit for irt_mz_extraction_window: 'Th' or 'ppm'

param.name: stop_after_feature
param.label: Stop finding after feature (ordered by intensity; -1 means do not stop)

param.name: min_peak_width
param.label: Minimal peak width (s), discard all peaks below this value (-1 means no action)

param.name: peak_integration
param.label: Calculate the peak area and height either the smoothed or the raw chromatogram data

param.name: background_subtraction
param.label: Remove background from peak signal using estimated noise levels
param.help: The 'original' method is only provided for historical purposes, please use the 'exact' method and set parameters using the PeakIntegrator: settings. The same original or smoothed chromatogram specified by peak_integration will be used for background estimation

param.name: recalculate_peaks
param.label: Tries to get better peak picking by looking at peak consistency of all picked peaks
param.help: Tries to use the consensus (median) peak border if the variation within the picked peaks is too large

param.name: use_precursors
param.label: Use precursor chromatogram for peak picking (note that this may lead to precursor signal driving the peak picking)

param.name: use_consensus
param.label: Use consensus peak boundaries when computing transition group picking (if false, compute independent peak boundaries for each transition)

param.name: recalculate_peaks_max_z
param.label: Determines the maximal Z-Score (difference measured in standard deviations) that is considered too large for peak boundaries
param.help: If the Z-Score is above this value, the median is used for peak boundaries (default value 1.0)

param.name: minimal_quality
param.label: Only if compute_peak_quality is set, this parameter will not consider peaks below this quality threshold

param.name: resample_boundary
param.label: For computing peak quality, how many extra seconds should be sample left and right of the actual peak

param.name: compute_peak_quality
param.label: Tries to compute a quality value for each peakgroup and detect outlier transitions
param.help: The resulting score is centered around zero and values above 0 are generally good and below -1 or -2 are usually bad

param.name: compute_peak_shape_metrics
param.label: Calculates various peak shape metrics
param.help: (e.g., tailing) that can be used for downstream QC/QA

param.name: compute_total_mi
param.label: Compute mutual information metrics for individual transitions that can be used for OpenSWATH/IPF scoring

param.name: boundary_selection_method
param.label: Method to use when selecting the best boundaries for peaks

param.name: sgolay_frame_length
param.label: The number of subsequent data points used for smoothing
param.help: This number has to be uneven. If it is not, 1 will be added

param.name: sgolay_polynomial_order
param.label: Order of the polynomial that is fitted

param.name: gauss_width
param.label: Gaussian width in seconds, estimated peak size

param.name: use_gauss
param.label: Use Gaussian filter for smoothing (alternative is Savitzky-Golay filter)

param.name: peak_width
param.label: Force a certain minimal peak_width on the data
param.help: (e.g. extend the peak at least by this amount on both sides) in seconds. -1 turns this feature off

param.name: signal_to_noise
param.label: Signal-to-noise threshold at which a peak will not be extended any more
param.help: Note that setting this too high (e.g. 1.0) can lead to peaks whose flanks are not fully captured

param.name: write_sn_log_messages
param.label: Write out log messages of the signal-to-noise estimator in case of sparse windows or median in rightmost histogram bin

param.name: report_sn
param.label: Also report the apex signal-to-noise ratio for each picked peak (as an additional 'SN' FloatDataArray on the picked chromatogram)
param.help: Forces initialization of the S/N estimator even if 'signal_to_noise' is 0

param.name: remove_overlapping_peaks
param.label: Try to remove overlapping peaks during peak picking

param.name: method
param.label: Which method to choose for chromatographic peak-picking (OpenSWATH legacy on raw data, corrected picking on smoothed chromatogram or Crawdad on smoothed chromatogram)

param.name: integration_type
param.label: The integration technique to use in integratePeak() and estimateBackground() which uses either the summed intensity, integration by Simpson's rule or trapezoidal integration

param.name: baseline_type
param.label: The baseline type to use in estimateBackground() based on the peak boundaries
param.help: A rectangular baseline shape is computed based either on the minimal intensity of the peak boundaries, the maximum intensity or the average intensity (base_to_base)

param.name: fit_EMG
param.label: Fit the chromatogram/spectrum to the EMG peak model

param.name: dia_extraction_window
param.label: DIA extraction window in Th or ppm

param.name: dia_extraction_unit
param.label: DIA extraction window unit

param.name: dia_centroided
param.label: Use centroided DIA data

param.name: dia_byseries_intensity_min
param.label: DIA b/y series minimum intensity to conside

param.name: dia_byseries_ppm_diff
param.label: DIA b/y series minimal difference in ppm to conside

param.name: dia_nr_isotopes
param.label: DIA number of isotopes to conside

param.name: dia_nr_charges
param.label: DIA number of charges to conside

param.name: peak_before_mono_max_ppm_diff
param.label: DIA maximal difference in ppm to count a peak at lower m/z when searching for evidence that a peak might not be monoisotopic

param.name: max_iteration
param.label: Maximum number of iterations using by Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm

param.name: init_mom
param.label: Initialize parameters using method of moments estimators

param.name: use_shape_score
param.label: Use the shape score (this score measures the similarity in shape of the transitions using a cross-correlation)

param.name: use_coelution_score
param.label: Use the coelution score (this score measures the similarity in coelution of the transitions using a cross-correlation)

param.name: use_rt_score
param.label: Use the retention time score (this score measure the difference in retention time)

param.name: use_library_score
param.label: Use the library score

param.name: use_intensity_score
param.label: Use the intensity score

param.name: use_nr_peaks_score
param.label: Use the number of peaks score

param.name: use_total_xic_score
param.label: Use the total XIC score

param.name: use_total_mi_score
param.label: Use the total MI score

param.name: use_sn_score
param.label: Use the SN (signal to noise) score

param.name: use_mi_score
param.label: Use the MI (mutual information) score

param.name: use_dia_scores
param.label: Use the DIA (SWATH) scores
param.help: If turned off, will not use fragment ion spectra for scoring

param.name: use_ms1_correlation
param.label: Use the correlation scores with the MS1 elution profiles

param.name: use_ion_mobility_scores

param.name: use_ms1_fullscan
param.label: Use the full MS1 scan at the peak apex for scoring (ppm accuracy of precursor and isotopic pattern)

param.name: use_ms1_mi
param.label: Use the MS1 MI score

param.name: use_uis_scores
param.label: Use UIS scores for peptidoform identification

param.name: use_peak_shape_metrics
param.label: Use peak shape metrics for scoring

param.name: use_ionseries_scores
param.label: Use MS2-level b/y ion-series scores for peptidoform identification

param.name: use_ms2_isotope_scores
